issues.description: Public class name mismatch: the template file template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java declares a public class named 'AnimalFarm' (line 3) while the problem statement UML and the reference solution expect a public class named 'Farm' (problem_statement.md UML: lines 16-22; solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java declares 'public class Farm' at line 6). This mismatch causes Java compilation errors (public class name must match the file name) and will confuse students who are instructed to implement/extend a class named Farm according to the UML.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the public class in template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java from 'AnimalFarm' to 'Farm' so the public class name matches the file name. Remove the duplicated/illegal nested 'package' declaration blocks and ensure there is a single valid package declaration at the top of the file. Structure the class to match the UML (declare private List<Animal> animals, no-arg constructor initializing an ArrayList, getters/setters, addAnimal, feedAllAnimals, singFarmSong and private singFarmSongVerse) leaving method bodies as stubs/TODOs where appropriate for student implementation. This will restore compilability and align the template with the problem statement and tests while preserving pedagogical content.
